title: 3.5 New ways of asking questions
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 0/6 段落 · 審校済み 0


1
Traditional surveys are closed, boring, and removed from life. Now we can ask questions that are more open, more fun, and more embedded in life.



2The total survey error framework encourages researchers to think about survey research as a two-part process: recruiting respondents and asking them questions. In section 3.4, I discussed how the digital age changes how we recruit respondents, and now I’ll discuss how it enables researchers to ask questions in new ways. These new approaches can be used with either probability samples or non-probability samples.


3A survey mode is the environment in which the questions are asked, and it can have important impacts on measurement (Couper 2011). In the first era of survey research, the most common mode was face to face, while in the second era, it was telephone. Some researchers view the third era of survey research as just an expansion of survey modes to include computers and mobile phones. However, the digital age is more than just a change in the pipes through which questions and answers flow. Instead, the transition from analog to digital enables—and will likely require—researchers to change how we ask questions.


4A study by Michael Schober and colleagues (2015) illustrates the benefits of adjusting traditional approaches to better match digital-age communication systems. In this study, Schober and colleagues compared different approaches to asking people questions via a mobile phone. They compared collecting data via voice conversations, which would have been a natural translation of second-era approaches, to collecting data via many microsurveys sent through text messages, an approach with no obvious precedent. They found that microsurveys sent through text messages led to higher-quality data than voice interviews. In other words, simply transferring the old approach into the new medium did not lead to the highest-quality data. Instead, by thinking clearly about the capabilities and social norms around mobile phones, Schober and colleagues were able to develop a better way of asking questions that lead to higher-quality responses.


5There are many dimensions along which researchers can categorize survey modes, but I think the most critical feature of digital-age survey modes is that they are computer-administered, rather than interviewer-administered (as in telephone and face-to-face surveys). Taking human interviewers out of the data collection process offers enormous benefits and introduces some drawbacks. In terms of benefits, removing human interviewers can reduce social desirability bias, the tendency for respondents to try to present themselves in the best possible way by, for example, under-reporting stigmatized behavior (e.g., illegal drug use) and over-reporting encouraged behavior (e.g., voting) (Kreuter, Presser, and Tourangeau 2008). Removing human interviewers can also eliminate interviewer effects, the tendency for responses to be influenced in subtle ways by the characteristics of the human interviewer (West and Blom 2016). In addition to potentially improving accuracy for some types of questions, removing human interviewers also dramatically reduces costs—interview time is one of the biggest expenses in survey research—and increases flexibility because respondents can participate whenever they want, not just when an interviewer is available. However, removing the human interviewer also creates some challenges. In particular, interviewers can develop a rapport with respondents that can increase participation rates, clarify confusing questions, and maintain respondents’ engagement while they slog through a long (potentially tedious) questionnaire (Garbarski, Schaeffer, and Dykema 2016). Thus, switching from an interviewer-administered survey mode to a computer-administered one creates both opportunities and challenges.


6Next, I’ll describe two approaches showing how researchers can take advantage of the tools of the digital age to ask questions differently: measuring internal states at a more appropriate time and place through ecological momentary assessment (section 3.5.1) and combining the strengths of open-ended and closed-ended survey questions through wiki surveys (section 3.5.2). However, the move toward computer-administered, ubiquitous asking will also mean that we need to design ways of asking that are more enjoyable for participants, a process sometimes called gamification (section 3.5.3).

title: 3.3.3 Cost
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 0/4 段落 · 審校済み 0



3.3.3 Cost

1
Surveys are not free, and this is a real constraint.



2So far, I’ve briefly reviewed the total survey error framework, which itself is the subject of book-length treatments (Weisberg 2005; Groves et al. 2009). Although this framework is comprehensive, it generally causes researchers to overlook an important factor: cost. Although cost—which can be measured by either time or money—is rarely explicitly discussed by academic researchers, it is a real constraint that should not be ignored. In fact, cost is fundamental to the entire process of survey research (Groves 2004): it is the reason researchers interview a sample of people rather than an entire population. A single-minded devotion to minimizing error while completely ignoring cost is not always in our best interest.


3The limitations of an obsession with reducing error are illustrated by the landmark project of Scott Keeter and colleagues (2000) on the effects of expensive field operations on reducing nonresponse in telephone surveys. Keeter and colleagues ran two simultaneous studies, one using “standard” recruitment procedures and one using “rigorous” recruitment procedures. The difference between the two studies was the amount of effort that went into contacting respondents and encouraging them to participate. For example, in the study with “rigorous” recruitment, researchers called the sampled households more frequently and over a longer period of time and made extra callbacks if participants initially refused to participate. These extra efforts did in fact produce a lower rate of nonresponse, but they added to the cost substantially. The study using “rigorous” procedures was twice as expensive and eight times slower. And, in the end, both studies produced essentially identical estimates. This project, as well as subsequent replications with similar findings (Keeter et al. 2006), should lead you to wonder: are we better off with two reasonable surveys or one pristine survey? What about 10 reasonable surveys or one pristine survey? What about 100 reasonable surveys or one pristine survey? At some point, cost advantages must outweigh vague, nonspecific concerns about quality.


4As I’ll show in this rest of the chapter, many of the opportunities created by the digital age are not about making estimates that obviously have lower error. Rather, these opportunities are about estimating different quantities and about making estimates faster and cheaper, even with possibly higher errors. Researchers who insist on a single-minded obsession with minimizing error at the expense of other dimensions of quality are going to miss out on exciting opportunities. Given this background about the total survey error framework, we will now turn to three main areas of the third era of survey research: new approaches to representation (section 3.4), new approaches to measurement (section 3.5), and new strategies for combining surveys with big data sources (section 3.6).

title: 3.3.1 Representation
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 0/11 段落 · 審校済み 0



3.3.1 Representation

1
Representation is about making inferences from your respondents to your target population.



2In order to understand the kind of errors that can happen when inferring from respondents to the larger population, let’s consider the Literary Digest straw poll that tried to predict the outcome of the 1936 US presidential election. Although it happened more than 75 years ago, this debacle still has an important lesson to teach researchers today.


3Literary Digest was a popular general-interest magazine, and starting in 1920 they began running straw polls to predict the outcomes of presidential elections. To make these predictions, they would send ballots to lots of people and then simply tally up the ballots that were returned; Literary Digest proudly reported that the ballots they received were neither “weighted, adjusted, nor interpreted.” This procedure correctly predicted the winners of the elections in 1920, 1924, 1928 and 1932. In 1936, in the midst of the Great Depression, Literary Digest sent out ballots to 10 million people, whose names came predominantly from telephone directories and automobile registration records. Here’s how they described their methodology:


4
“THE DIGEST’s smooth-running machine moves with the swift precision of thirty years’ experience to reduce guesswork to hard facts … This week 500 pens scratched out more than a quarter of a million addresses a day. Every day, in a great room high above motor-ribboned Fourth Avenue, in New York, 400 workers deftly slide a million pieces of printed matter—enough to pave forty city blocks—into the addressed envelops [sic]. Every hour, in THE DIGEST’S own Post Office Substation, three chattering postage metering machines sealed and stamped the white oblongs; skilled postal employees flipped them into bulging mailsacks; fleet DIGEST trucks sped them to express mail-trains . . . Next week, the first answers from these ten million will begin the incoming tide of marked ballots, to be triple-checked, verified, five-times cross-classified and totaled. When the last figure has been totted and checked, if past experience is a criterion, the country will know to within a fraction of 1 percent the actual popular vote of forty million [voters].” (August 22, 1936)



5Literary Digest’s fetishization of size is instantly recognizable to any “big data” researcher today. Of the 10 million ballots distributed, an amazing 2.4 million were returned—that’s roughly 1,000 times larger than modern political polls. From these 2.4 million respondents, the verdict was clear: Alf Landon was going to defeat the incumbent Franklin Roosevelt. But, in fact, Roosevelt defeated Landon in a landslide. How could Literary Digest go wrong with so much data? Our modern understanding of sampling makes Literary Digest’s mistakes clear and helps us avoid making similar mistakes in the future.


6Thinking clearly about sampling requires us to consider four different groups of people (figure 3.2). The first group is the target population; this is the group that the researcher defines as the population of interest. In the case of Literary Digest, the target population was voters in the 1936 presidential election.


7After deciding on a target population, a researcher needs to develop a list of people that can be used for sampling. This list is called a sampling frame and the people on it are called the frame population. Ideally, the target population and the frame population would be exactly the same, but in practice this is often not the case. For example, in the case of Literary Digest, the frame population was the 10 million people whose names came predominately from telephone directories and automobile registration records. Differences between the target population and the frame population are called coverage error. Coverage error does not, by itself, guarantee problems. However, it can lead to coverage bias if people in the frame population are systematically different from people in the target population who are not in the frame population. This is, in fact, exactly what happened in the Literary Digest poll. The people in their frame population tended to be more likely to support Alf Landon, in part because they were wealthier (recall that both telephones and automobiles were relatively new and expensive in 1936). So, in the Literary Digest poll, coverage error led to coverage bias.


8

Figure 3.2: Representation errors.



9After defining the frame population, the next step is for a researcher to select the sample population; these are the people who the researcher will attempt to interview. If the sample has different characteristics than the frame population, then sampling can introduce sampling error. In the case of the Literary Digest fiasco, however, there actually was no sampling—the magazine to contact everyone in the frame population—and therefore there was no sampling error. Many researchers tend to focus on sampling error—this is typically the only kind of error captured by the margin of error reported in surveys—but the Literary Digest fiasco reminds us that we need to consider all sources of error, both random and systematic.


10Finally, after selecting a sample population, a researcher attempts to interview all its members. Those people who are successfully interviewed are called respondents. Ideally, the sample population and the respondents would be exactly the same, but in practice there is nonresponse. That is, people who are selected in the sample sometimes do not participate. If the people who respond are different from those who don’t respond, then there can be nonresponse bias. Nonresponse bias was the second main problem with the Literary Digest poll. Only 24% of the people who received a ballot responded, and it turned out that people who supported Landon were more likely to respond.


11Beyond just being an example to introduce the ideas of representation, the Literary Digest poll is an oft-repeated parable, cautioning researchers about the dangers of haphazard sampling. Unfortunately, I think that the lesson that many people draw from this story is the wrong one. The most common moral of the story is that researchers can’t learn anything from non-probability samples (i.e., samples without strict probability-based rules for selecting participants). But, as I’ll show later in this chapter, that’s not quite right. Instead, I think there are really two morals to this story; morals that are as true today as they were in 1936. First, a large amount of haphazardly collected data will not guarantee a good estimate. In general, having a large number of respondents decreases the variance of estimates, but it does not necessarily decrease the bias. With lots of data, researchers can sometimes get a precise estimate of the wrong thing; they can be precisely inaccurate (McFarland and McFarland 2015). The second main lesson from the Literary Digest fiasco is that researchers need to account for how their sample was collected when making estimates. In other words, because the sampling process in the Literary Digest poll was systematically skewed toward some respondents, researchers needed to use a more complex estimation process that weighted some respondents more than others. Later in this chapter, I’ll show you one such weighting procedure—post-stratification—that can enable you to make better estimates from haphazard samples.

title: 3.2 Asking versus observing
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 0/4 段落 · 審校済み 0


1
We are always going to need to ask people questions.



2Given that more and more of our behavior is captured in big data sources, such as government and business administrative data, some people might think that asking questions is a thing of the past. But, it’s not that simple. There are two main reasons that I think researchers will continue to ask people questions. First, as I discussed in chapter 2, there are real problems with the accuracy, completeness, and accessibility of many big data sources. Second, in addition to these practical reasons, there is more fundamental reason: there are some things that are very hard to learn from behavioral data—even perfect behavioral data. For example, some of the most important social outcomes and predictors are internal states, such as emotions, knowledge, expectations, and opinions. Internal states exist inside people’s heads, and sometimes the best way to learn about internal states is to ask.


3The practical and fundamental limitations of big data sources, and how they can be overcome with surveys, are illustrated by Moira Burke and Robert Kraut’s (2014) research on how the strength of friendships was impacted by interaction on Facebook. At the time, Burke was working at Facebook so she had complete access to one of the most massive and detailed records of human behavior ever created. But, even so, Burke and Kraut had to use surveys in order to answer their research question. Their outcome of interest—the subjective feeling of closeness between the respondent and her friend—is an internal state that only exists inside the respondent’s head. Further, in addition to using a survey to collect their outcome of interest, Burke and Kraut also had to use a survey to learn about potentially confounding factors. In particular, they wanted to separate the impact of communicating on Facebook from communication through other channels (e.g., email, phone, and face to face). Even though interactions through email and phone are automatically recorded, these traces were not available to Burke and Kraut so they had to collect them with a survey. Combining their survey data about friendship strength and non-Facebook interaction with the Facebook log data, Burke and Kraut concluded that communication via Facebook did in fact lead to increased feelings of closeness.


4As the work of Burke and Kraut illustrates, big data sources will not eliminate the need to ask people questions. In fact, I would draw the opposite lesson from this study: big data sources can actually increase the value of asking questions, as I will show throughout this chapter. Therefore, the best way to think about the relationship between asking and observing is that they are complements rather than substitutes; they are like peanut butter and jelly. When there is more peanut butter, people want more jelly; when there is more big data, I think people will want more surveys.

text:

6[, ] Algorithmic confounding was a problem with Google Flu Trends. Read the paper by Lazer et al. (2014), and write a short, clear email to an engineer at Google explaining the problem and offering an idea of how to fix it.






Tip日本語訳





アルゴリズム的混同はGoogle Flu Trendsにおける問題でした。Lazerら（2014）の論文を参照してください。そして、Googleのエンジニアに対して、この問題とその解決策のアイデアについて簡潔かつ明確なメールを書くようにしてください。









Note理解のポイント





要点:アルゴリズム的混同がGoogle Flu Trendsの問題であり、その解決策をエンジニアに提案する。





7[] Bollen, Mao, and Zeng (2011) claims that data from Twitter can be used to predict the stock market. This finding led to the creation of a hedge fund—Derwent Capital Markets—to invest in the stock market based on data collected from Twitter (Jordan 2010). What evidence would you want to see before putting your money in that fund?






Tip日本語訳





Bollen, Mao, and Zeng (2011) は、Twitter のデータを使用して株式市場を予測できると主張しています。この発見は、Twitter から収集したデータに基づいて株式市場に投資するヘッジファンド—Derwent Capital Markets—の設立につながりました（Jordan 2010）。そのファンドに資金を投入する前にどのような証拠を見たいと思いますか？









Note理解のポイント





要点:Twitterのデータから株式市場を予測できるという研究結果に基づくヘッジファンドへの投資前にどのような証拠が必要か。





8
[] While some public health advocates consider e-cigarettes an effective aid for smoking cessation, others warn about the potential risks, such as the high levels of nicotine. Imagine that a researcher decides to study public opinion toward e-cigarettes by collecting e-cigarettes-related Twitter posts and conducting sentiment analysis.

What are the three possible biases that you are most worried about in this study?

Clark et al. (2016) ran just such a study. First, they collected 850,000 tweets that used e-cigarette-related keywords from January 2012 through December 2014. Upon closer inspection, they realized that many of these tweets were automated (i.e., not produced by humans) and many of these automated tweets were essentially commercials. They developed a human detection algorithm to separate automated tweets from organic tweets. Using this human detect algorithm they found that 80% of tweets were automated. Does this finding change your answer to part (a)?
When they compared the sentiment in organic and automated tweets, they found that the automated tweets were more positive than organic tweets (6.17 versus 5.84). Does this finding change your answer to (b)?








Tip日本語訳





一部の公衆衛生擁護者は電子タバコが禁煙の効果的な支援ツールであると考えていますが、他の人々はニコチンの高濃度など潜在的なリスクについて警告しています。ある研究者が電子タバコに対する公衆の意見を調査するために、関連するツイートを集め、感情分析を行うことを決めました。この研究ではどのようなバイアスが最も懸念されるでしょうか。クラークら（2016）はまさにこのような研究を行いました。彼らは2012年1月から2014年12月までの期間に電子タバコに関連するキーワードを使用した85万件のツイートを集めました。詳細な調査により、これらのツイートの多くが自動生成されたもの（つまり人間によって生成されないもの）であり、その多くが実質的に広告であることがわかりました。彼らは人間生成のツイートと自動生成のツイートを分けるための人間検出アルゴリズムを開発しました。このアルゴリズムを使用して、ツイートの80%が自動生成であることがわかりました。この結果は、あなたが(a)の部分で答えた内容を変えるでしょうか。人間生成のツイートと自動生成のツイートの感情を比較すると、自動生成のツイートの方が人間生成のツイートよりもポジティブでした（6.17対5.84）。この結果は、あなたが(b)の部分で答えた内容を変えるでしょうか。









Note理解のポイント





要点:ツイートの自動生成によるバイアス、ポジティブな感情のバイアスが懸念される。





9
[] In November 2009, Twitter changed the question in the tweet box from “What are you doing?” to “What’s happening?” (https://blog.twitter.com/2009/whats-happening).

How do you think the change of prompts will affect who tweets and/or what they tweet?
Name one research project for which you would prefer the prompt “What are you doing?” Explain why.
Name one research project for which you would prefer the prompt “What’s happening?” Explain why.








Tip日本語訳





2009年11月、Twitterはツイートボックスの質問を「What are you doing?」から「What’s happening?」に変更しました（https://blog.twitter.com/2009/whats-happening）。 この質問の変更が誰がツイートするか、または彼らが何をツイートするかにどのような影響を与えると考えられますか？ 「What are you doing?」というプロンプトを好む研究プロジェクトの1つを挙げ、その理由を説明してください。 「What’s happening?」というプロンプトを好む研究プロジェクトの1つを挙げ、その理由を説明してください。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Twitterのプロンプト変更がツイート内容やユーザーに与える影響について考察し、それぞれのプロンプトを好む研究プロジェクトとその理由を述べよ。





10[] “Retweets” are often used to measure influence and spread of influence on Twitter. Initially, users had to copy and paste the tweet they liked, tag the original author with his/her handle, and manually type “RT” before the tweet to indicate that it was a retweet. Then, in 2009, Twitter added a “retweet” button. In June 2016, Twitter made it possible for users to retweet their own tweets (https://twitter.com/twitter/status/742749353689780224). Do you think these changes should affect how you use “retweets” in your research? Why or why not?






Tip日本語訳





「リツイート」は、Twitter上で影響力とその影響力を広げる度合いを測る際に頻繁に使用される。当初、ユーザーは好むツイートをコピーし、ペーストし、元の著者をハンドルでタグ付けし、「RT」という文字を手動でツイートの前に付ける必要があった。その後、2009年にTwitterは「リツイート」ボタンを追加した。そして2016年6月、Twitterはユーザーが自分のツイートをリツイートできるようにした（https://twitter.com/twitter/status/742749353689780224）。これらの変更は、あなたの研究における「リツイート」の使用に影響を与えるべきだと思いますか？なぜですか、またはなぜではないですか？









Note理解のポイント





要点:Twitterのリツイート機能の変更が研究におけるリツイートの使用に影響を与えるべきかどうか。





11
[, , , ] In a widely discussed paper, Michel and colleagues (2011) analyzed the content of more than five million digitized books in an attempt to identify long-term cultural trends. The data that they used has now been released as the Google NGrams dataset, and so we can use the data to replicate and extend some of their work.
In one of the many results in the paper, Michel and colleagues argued that we are forgetting faster and faster. For a particular year, say “1883,” they calculated the proportion of 1-grams published in each year between 1875 and 1975 that were “1883”. They reasoned that this proportion is a measure of the interest in events that happened in that year. In their figure 3a, they plotted the usage trajectories for three years: 1883, 1910, and 1950. These three years share a common pattern: little use before that year, then a spike, then decay. Next, to quantify the rate of decay for each year, Michel and colleagues calculated the “half-life” of each year for all years between 1875 and 1975. In their figure 3a (inset), they showed that the half-life of each year is decreasing, and they argued that this means that we are forgetting the past faster and faster. They used Version 1 of the English language corpus, but subsequently Google has released a second version of the corpus. Please read all the parts of the question before you begin coding.
This activity will give you practice writing reusable code, interpreting results, and data wrangling (such as working with awkward files and handling missing data). This activity will also help you get up and running with a rich and interesting dataset.

Get the raw data from the Google Books NGram Viewer website. In particular, you should use version 2 of the English language corpus, which was released on July 1, 2012. Uncompressed, this file is 1.4GB.
Recreate the main part of figure 3a of Michel et al. (2011). To recreate this figure, you will need two files: the one you downloaded in part (a) and the “total counts” file, which you can use to convert the raw counts into proportions. Note that the total counts file has a structure that may make it a bit hard to read in. Does version 2 of the NGram data produce similar results to those presented in Michel et al. (2011), which are based on version 1 data?
Now check your graph against the graph created by the NGram Viewer.
Recreate figure 3a (main figure), but change the \(y\)-axis to be the raw mention count (not the rate of mentions).
Does the difference between (b) and (d) lead you to reevaluate any of the results of Michel et al. (2011). Why or why not?
Now, using the proportion of mentions, replicate the inset of figure 3a. That is, for each year between 1875 and 1975, calculate the half-life of that year. The half-life is defined to be the number of years that pass before the proportion of mentions reaches half its peak value. Note that Michel et al. (2011) do something more complicated to estimate the half-life—see section III.6 of the Supporting Online Information—but they claim that both approaches produce similar results. Does version 2 of the NGram data produce similar results to those presented in Michel et al. (2011), which are based on version 1 data? (Hint: Don’t be surprised if it doesn’t.)
Were there any years that were outliers such as years that were forgotten particularly quickly or particularly slowly? Briefly speculate about possible reasons for that pattern and explain how you identified the outliers.
Now replicate this result for version 2 of the NGrams data in Chinese, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Russian and Spanish.
Comparing across all languages, were there any years that were outliers, such as years that were forgotten particularly quickly or particularly slowly? Briefly speculate about possible reasons for that pattern.








Tip日本語訳





Michelら（2011）は、500万冊以上のデジタル化された本の内容を分析し、長期的な文化的トレンドを特定しようと試みた論文において、我々は過去の出来事に対する関心度を測る指標として、特定の年（例えば「1883」）が各年間に出版された1-グラムの割合を計算した。彼らは、その割合がその年の出来事に対する関心度を示す指標であると主張し、1883年、1910年、1950年の使用動向をプロットした。これらの3つの年は、その年以前は使用頻度が低く、その後ピークを迎え、徐々に減少するという共通のパターンを示した。次に、各年の減少率を量化的に評価するために、1875年から1975年までの各年の「半減期」を計算した。彼らは、その半減期が減少していることを示し、これは我々が過去を忘れている速度が速くなっていることを意味すると主張した。彼らは英語版コーパスのバージョン1を使用したが、その後Googleはコーパスのバージョン2をリリースした。この活動では、再利用可能なコードの作成、結果の解釈、データの取り扱い（不適切なファイルや欠損データの処理など）の練習を行う。また、豊富で興味深いデータセットとの対話も可能となる。 Google Books NGram Viewerウェブサイトから生データを取得せよ。特に、2012年7月1日にリリースされた英語版コーパスのバージョン2を使用せよ。このファイルは圧縮されていない状態で1.4GBである。Michelら（2011）の図3aの主要部分を再現せよ。この図を再現するには、ダウンロードしたファイルと「総数」ファイルが必要である。総数ファイルは読み込みにくい構造を持っている可能性があることに注意せよ。NGramデータのバージョン2は、バージョン1に基づくMichelら（2011）の結果と似た結果を生むか確認せよ。グラフをNGram Viewerによって作成されたものと比較せよ。図3a（主図）を再現せよが、(y)軸を言及回数の原始値（割合ではなく）に変更せよ。図（b）と図（d）の違いは、Michelら（2011）の結果を再評価する必要があるか？なぜか、なぜなら？言及割合を使用して、図3aの挿絵を再現せよ。すなわち、1875年から1975年までの各年の半減期を計算せよ。半減期は、言及割合がピークの半分になるまでにかかる年数を定義する。Michelら（2011）はより複雑な方法で半減期を推定しているが、両方のアプローチは似たような結果を生むと主張している。NGramデータのバージョン2は、バージョン1に基づくMichelら（2011）の結果と似た結果を生むか？（ヒント：一致しない場合でも驚かないように。）どの年が異常値（特に早く忘れられたり、遅く忘れられたり）だったかを特定し、そのパターンの理由を簡単に推測せよ。次に、中国語、フランス語、ドイツ語、ヘブライ語、イタリア語、ロシア語、スペイン語のNGramsデータのバージョン2に対して、この結果を再現せよ。すべての言語を比較した場合、どの年が異常値（特に早く忘れられたり、遅く忘れられたり）だったかを特定し、そのパターンの理由を簡単に推測せよ。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Michelら（2011）は、デジタル化された本のデータを用いて、我々が過去を忘れている速度が増していることを示した。





12
[, , , ] Penney (2016) explored whether the widespread publicity about NSA/PRISM surveillance (i.e., the Snowden revelations) in June 2013 was associated with a sharp and sudden decrease in traffic to Wikipedia articles on topics that raise privacy concerns. If so, this change in behavior would be consistent with a chilling effect resulting from mass surveillance. The approach of Penney (2016) is sometimes called an interrupted time series design, and it is related to the approaches described in section 2.4.3.
To choose the topic keywords, Penney referred to the list used by the US Department of Homeland Security for tracking and monitoring social media. The DHS list categorizes certain search terms into a range of issues, i.e., “Health Concern,” “Infrastructure Security,” and “Terrorism.” For the study group, Penney used the 48 keywords related to “Terrorism” (see appendix table 8). He then aggregated Wikipedia article view counts on a monthly basis for the corresponding 48 Wikipedia articles over a 32-month period, from the beginning of January 2012 to the end of August 2014. To strengthen his argument, he also created several comparison groups by tracking article views on other topics.
Now, you are going to replicate and extend Penney (2016). All the raw data that you will need for this activity is available from Wikipedia. Or you can get it from the R-package wikipediatrend (Meissner and R Core Team 2016). When you write up your responses, please note which data source you used. (Note that this same activity also appears in chapter 6.) This activity will give you practice in data wrangling and thinking about natural experiments in big data sources. It will also get you up and running with a potentially interesting data source for future projects.

Read Penney (2016) and replicate his figure 2 which shows the page views for “Terrorism”-related pages before and after the Snowden revelations. Interpret the findings.
Next, replicate figure 4A, which compares the study group (“Terrorism”-related articles) with a comparator group using keywords categorized under “DHS & Other Agencies” from the DHS list (see appendix table 10 and footnote 139). Interpret the findings.
In part (b) you compared the study group with one comparator group. Penney also compared with two other comparator groups: “Infrastructure Security” related articles (appendix table 11) and popular Wikipedia pages (appendix table 12). Come up with an alternative comparator group, and test whether the findings from part (b) are sensitive to your choice of comparator group. Which choice of makes most sense? Why?
Penney stated that keywords relating to “Terrorism” were used to select the Wikipedia articles because the US government cited terrorism as a key justification for its online surveillance practices. As a check of these 48 “Terrorism”-related keywords, Penney (2016) also conducted a survey on MTurk, asking respondents to rate each of ht keywords in terms of Government Trouble, Privacy-Sensitive, and Avoidance (appendix table 7 and 8). Replicate the survey on MTurk and compare your results.
Based on the results in part (d) and your reading of the article, do you agree with Penney’s choice of topic keywords in the study group? Why or why not? If not, what would you suggest instead?








Tip日本語訳





Penney (2016) 調査したのは、2013年6月に広く公表されたNSA/PRISM監視（Snowden漏洩）がプライバシーに関する懸念を引き起こすWikipedia記事へのトラフィックに急激な減少をもたらしたかどうかである。この変化は大量監視による寒蟄効果の一環である可能性がある。Penneyのアプローチは中断時間系列設計と呼ばれ、セクション2.4.3で説明されているアプローチに関連している。トピックキーワードの選択には、米国国土安全保障省がソーシャルメディアの追跡とモニタリングのために使用しているリストを参照した。研究グループでは、「テロリズム」に関連する48のキーワードを使用し、それに対応する48のWikipedia記事のページビュー数を2012年1月から2014年8月までの32ヶ月間月ごとに集計した。さらに、他のトピックの記事のページビューを追跡することで比較グループを作成した。この活動では、データの取り扱いやビッグデータソースでの自然実験の思考を練習し、今後のプロジェクトで使用できる可能性のある興味深いデータソースとの対話を行う。 Penney (2016) を読み、Snowden漏洩前後での「テロリズム」関連ページのページビューを示す図2を再現し、その結果を解釈する。次に、DHSリストの「DHS & Other Agencies」カテゴリのキーワードを使用した比較グループとの比較を示す図4Aを再現し、その結果を解釈する。部分(b)では、一つの比較グループと研究グループを比較したが、Penneyは「インフラセキュリティ」関連記事と人気のあるWikipediaページとの比較も行った。異なる比較グループを選択した場合、部分(b)の結果がどの程度影響を受けるかを検討し、最も意味のある選択は何か、なぜそれが最も意味があるのかを説明する。Penneyは「テロリズム」関連キーワードを選んだ理由として、アメリカ政府がオンライン監視の正当化としてテロリズムを挙げていることを挙げている。PenneyはMTurkでこれらの48の「テロリズム」関連キーワードに対する調査を行い、各キーワードに対する「政府問題」「プライバシー感度」「避難」の評価を行った。自身でMTurkで同様の調査を行い、結果を比較する。部分(d)の結果とPenneyの論文を読んだ上で、Penneyのトピックキーワードの選択に同意するか、なぜ同意するか、またはなぜしないか、代わりに何を提案するかを述べる。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Penney (2016) は、Snowden漏洩がプライバシー関連のWikipedia記事へのアクセスに影響を与えたかどうかを調査し、その方法と結果を再現・拡張する。





13[] Efrati (2016) reported, based on confidential information, that “total sharing” on Facebook had declined by about 5.5% year over year while “original broadcast sharing” was down 21% year over year. This decline was particularly acute with Facebook users under 30 years of age. The report attributed the decline to two factors. One is the growth in the number of “friends” people have on Facebook. The other is that some sharing activity has shifted to messaging and to competitors such as Snapchat. The report also revealed the several tactics Facebook had tried to boost sharing, including News Feed algorithm tweaks that make original posts more prominent, as well as periodic reminders of the original posts with the “On This Day” feature. What implications, if any, do these findings have for researchers who want to use Facebook as a data source?






Tip日本語訳





Efrati（2016）は、機密情報に基づいて、「完全共有」が年率約5.5%減少し、「オリジナル放送共有」が年率21%減少したと報告した。この減少は特に30歳未満のFacebookユーザーにおいて顕著であり、その原因として「友達」の数の増加と一部の共有活動がメッセージングやSnapchatなどの競合他社に移行していることが挙げられた。また、Facebookが共有を促進するために試みたいくつかの戦略も明らかにされ、その中にはオリジナル投稿をより目立つようにするためのニュースフィードアルゴリズムの調整や、「今日は」機能による定期的なオリジナル投稿の思い出させなどが含まれていた。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Facebookの「完全共有」が5.5%、「オリジナル放送共有」が21%減少しており、これは「友達」の増加と他のプラットフォームへの移行が原因とされる。





14[] What is the difference between a sociologist and a historian? According to Goldthorpe (1991), the main difference is control over data collection. Historians are forced to use relics, whereas sociologists can tailor their data collection to specific purposes. Read Goldthorpe (1991). How is the difference between sociology and history related to the idea of custommades and readymades?






Tip日本語訳





社会学者と歴史家の違いは何でしょうか？ゴールドソープ（1991）によれば、主な違いはデータ収集に対する制御力にあります。歴史家は遺物を使用せざるを得ないのに対し、社会学者はデータ収集を特定の目的に合わせて調整することができます。ゴールドソープ（1991）を参照してください。社会学と歴史の違いがカスタムメイドとオフザラックの概念に関係しているのはなぜでしょうか？









Note理解のポイント





要点:社会学者と歴史家の主な違いはデータ収集の制御力であり、歴史家は遺物に依存せざるを得ないのに対し、社会学者はデータ収集を特定の目的に合わせて調整できる。





15
[] This builds on the previous quesiton.Goldthorpe (1991) drew a number of critical responses, including one from Nicky Hart (1994) that challenged Goldthorpe’s devotion to tailor made data. To clarify the potential limitations of tailor-made data, Hart described the Affluent Worker Project, a large survey to measure the relationship between social class and voting that was conducted by Goldthorpe and colleagues in the mid-1960s. As one might expect from a scholar who favored designed data over found data, the Affluent Worker Project collected data that were tailored to address a recently proposed theory about the future of social class in an era of increasing living standards. But, Goldthorpe and colleagues somehow “forgot” to collect information about the voting behavior of women. Here’s how Nicky Hart (1994) summarized the whole episode:

“… it [is] difficult to avoid the conclusion that women were omitted because this ‘tailor made’ dataset was confined by a paradigmatic logic which excluded female experience. Driven by a theoretical vision of class consciousness and action as male preoccupations … , Goldthorpe and his colleagues constructed a set of empirical proofs which fed and nurtured their own theoretical assumptions instead of exposing them to a valid test of adequacy.”

Hart continued:

“The empirical findings of the Affluent Worker Project tell us more about the masculinist values of mid-century sociology than they inform the processes of stratification, politics and material life.”

Can you think of other examples where tailor-made data collection has the biases of the data collector built into it? How does this compare to algorithmic confounding? What implications might this have for when researchers should use readymades and when they should use custommades?







Tip日本語訳





これは前問につづくものである。Goldthorpe (1991) は多くの批判的な反応を引き起こし、その中には Nicky Hart (1994) のある反論が含まれていた。Hart は、Goldthorpe のカスタムデータへの献身を疑問視し、社会階級と投票の関係を測定するために1960年代半ばに Goldthorpe と同僚によって実施された大規模な調査「裕福な労働者プロジェクト」を例に挙げた。このプロジェクトは、生活水準の向上という時代背景の中で社会階級の将来に関する最近提唱された理論に対応するように設計されたデータを集めた。しかし、男性中心の理論によって女性の投票行動に関する情報が意図的に省かれたことが明らかになった。Nicky Hart (1994) は次のように要約した： 「… 女性が省かれたのは、このカスタムデータセットが女性の経験を排除するパラダイム論理によって制約されていたからだと避けるのが難しい。クラス意識と行動を男性の関心事と見なす理論的ビジョンに駆動されて、Goldthorpe と同僚は自らの理論的前提を検証するのではなく、それを養い育てた一連の実証的証拠を構築した。」 Hart はさらに次のように述べた： 「裕福な労働者プロジェクトの実証的発見は、中世紀の社会学における男性中心主義の価値観を我々に教えるよりも、階層化、政治、物質的生活の過程を我々に教えるものではない。」 カスタムデータ収集にデータ収集者のバイアスが組み込まれる他の例を思いつくことができるだろうか？これはアルゴリズム的混同行の比較とはどのように異なるのか？研究者が既製品を使用すべきときとカスタム製品を使用すべきときとはどのような違いがあるのか？









Note理解のポイント





要点:Nicky Hartは、Goldthorpeの「裕福な労働者プロジェクト」が女性の投票行動に関する情報を意図的に省いたことを指摘し、データ収集者のバイアスがカスタムデータに組み込まれる可能性を示している。





16
[] In this chapter, I have contrasted data collected by researchers for researchers with administrative records created by companies and governments. Some people call these administrative records “found data,” which they contrast with “designed data.” It is true that administrative records are found by researchers, but they are also highly designed. For example, modern tech companies work very hard to collect and curate their data. Thus, these administrative records are both found and designed, it just depends on your perspective (figure 2.12).


Figure 2.12: The picture is both a duck and a rabbit; what you see depends on your perspective. Big data sources are both found and designed; again, what you see depends on your perspective. For example, the call data records collected by a mobile-phone company are found data from the perspective of a researcher. But, these exact same records are designed data from the perspective of someone working in the billing department of the phone company. Source: Popular Science Monthly (1899)/Wikimedia Commons.

Provide an example of data source where seeing it both as found and designed is helpful when using that data source for research.







Tip日本語訳





この章では、研究者が他の研究者のために収集したデータと、企業や政府が作成した行政記録を対比しました。一部の人々は、これらの行政記録を「見つけたデータ」と呼び、これと「設計されたデータ」を対比しています。確かに行政記録は研究者が見つけますが、それらはまた非常に設計されています。たとえば、現代のテクノロジー企業はデータの収集とキュレーションに非常に努力を払います。したがって、これらの行政記録は見つけたものであり、設計されたものでもあり、視点によるところが大きい（図2.12）。 図2.12：この絵は同時にダックとラビットとして見えます；あなたが何を見るかは視点によるところが大きい。ビッグデータのソースは見つけたものであり、設計されたものでもあります；また、あなたが何を見るかは視点によるところが大きい。たとえば、モバイル電話会社が収集した通話データレコードは、研究者の視点からは見つけたデータですが、電話会社の請求部門で働く人々の視点からは設計されたデータです。出典：Popular Science Monthly (1899)/Wikimedia Commons。 見つけたデータと設計されたデータの両方としてそのデータソースを認識することが、そのデータソースを研究に使用する際に役立つ例を提供してください。









Note理解のポイント





要点:行政記録は研究者から見れば見つけたデータだが、企業や政府から見れば設計されたデータであり、視点によって異なる。





17[] In a thoughtful essay, Christian Sandvig and Eszter Hargittai (2015) split digital research into two broad categories depending on whether the digital system is an “instrument” or “object of study.” An example of the first kind—where the system is an instrument—is the research by Bengtsson and colleagues (2011) on using mobile-phone data to track migration after the earthquake in Haiti in 2010. An example of the second kind—where the system is an object of study—is research by Jensen (2007) on how the introduction of mobile phones throughout Kerala, India impacted the functioning of the market for fish. I find this distinction helpful because it clarifies that studies using digital data sources can have quite different goals even if they are using the same kind of data source. In order to further clarify this distinction, describe four studies that you’ve seen: two that use a digital system as an instrument and two that use a digital system as an object of study. You can use examples from this chapter if you want.






Tip日本語訳





クリスチャン・サンドヴィグとエスター・ハーギッタイ（2015）は、洞察に富む論考において、デジタルシステムが「道具」として使用されるか「研究対象」となるかによって、デジタル研究を大きく2つのカテゴリーに分類した。デジタルシステムが「道具」として使用される例としては、ベンクトソンら（2011）による2010年のハイチ地震後の移動をモバイル電話データで追跡する研究がある。一方、デジタルシステムが「研究対象」となる例としては、ジェンセン（2007）によるインドケララ州での携帯電話の導入が魚市場の機能にどのような影響を与えたかを研究する例がある。この区別は、同じ種類のデータソースを使用していても、研究の目的が全く異なる場合があることを明確にするため、非常に役立つ。









Note理解のポイント





要点:デジタルシステムが「道具」として使用される研究と「研究対象」となる研究の違いを示し、前者の例としてハイチ地震後の移動追跡研究、後者の例としてインドケララ州での携帯電話導入の影響研究を挙げた。







 Back to top

title: Mathematical notes
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 53/53 段落 · 審校済み 0


1In this appendix, I will summarize some ideas about making causal inference from non-experimental data in a slightly more mathematical form. There are two main approaches: the causal graph framework, most associated with Judea Pearl and colleagues, and the potential outcomes framework, most associated with Donald Rubin and colleagues. I will introduce the potential outcomes framework because it is more closely connected to the ideas in the mathematical notes at the end of chapter 3 and 4. For more on the causal graphs framework, I recommend Pearl, Glymour, and Jewell (2016) (introductory) and Pearl (2009) (advanced). For a book-length treatment of causal inference that combines the potential outcomes framework and the causal graph framework, I recommend Morgan and Winship (2014).






Tip日本語訳





この付録では、非実験データから因果推論を行うためのいくつかのアイデアをやや数学的な形式でまとめます。主なアプローチは2つあり、一つはジュデア・ペアルと同僚たちが主に関連付けられている因果グラフフレームワーク、もう一つはドナルド・ルビンと同僚たちが主に関連付けられている潜在結果フレームワークです。私は数学的なノートが第3章と第4章の終わりにあるアイデアとより密接に関連しているため、潜在結果フレームワークを紹介します。因果グラフフレームワークについてさらに詳しく知りたい場合は、ペアル、グリーモア、ジュエル（2016）（入門）とペアル（2009）（高度）を推奨します。潜在結果フレームワークと因果グラフフレームワークを組み合わせた因果推論に関する本格的な取り組みについては、モーガンとウィンシップ（2014）を推奨します。









Note理解のポイント





要点:非実験データからの因果推論の2つの主要アプローチとそれぞれの代表的な文献を紹介する。





2The goal of this appendix is to help you get comfortable with the notation and style of the potential outcomes tradition so that you can transition to some of the more technical material written on this topic. First, I’ll describe the potential outcomes framework. Then, I’ll use it to further discuss natural experiments like the one by Angrist (1990) on the effect of military service on earnings. This appendix draws heavily on Imbens and Rubin (2015).






Tip日本語訳





この付録の目的は、潜在的結果アプローチの表記法とスタイルに慣れ親しんでもらい、このトピックに関するより技術的な資料に移行できるようにすることである。まず、潜在結果フレームワークを説明し、次にAngrist (1990)による兵役が収入に及ぼす影響に関する自然実験のようなものをさらに議論する。この付録はImbens and Rubin (2015)に大きく依存している。









Note理解のポイント





要点:潜在的結果アプローチの表記法とスタイルに慣れ、Angrist (1990)の自然実験を用いた兵役の収入への影響の議論を行う付録で、Imbens and Rubin (2015)に多く依拠している。





3Potential outcomes framework






Tip日本語訳





潜在的結果枠組み









Note理解のポイント





要点:潜在的結果枠組みが主題である





4The potential outcomes framework has three main elements: units, treatments, and potential outcomes. In order to illustrate these elements, let’s consider a stylized version of the question addressed in Angrist (1990): What is the effect of military service on earnings? In this case, we can define the units to be people eligible for the 1970 draft in the United States, and we can index these people by \(i = 1, \ldots, N\). The treatments in this case can be “serving in the military” or “not serving in the military.” I’ll call these the treatment and control conditions, and I’ll write \(W_i = 1\) if person \(i\) is in the treatment condition and \(W_i = 0\) if person \(i\) is in the control condition. Finally, the potential outcomes are bit more conceptually difficult because they involve “potential” outcomes; things that could have happened. For each person eligible for the 1970 draft, we can imagine the amount that they would have earned in 1978 if they served in the military, which I will call \(Y_i(1)\), and the amount that they would have earned in 1978 if they did not serve in the military, which I will call \(Y_i(0)\). In the potential outcomes framework, \(Y_i(1)\) and \(Y_i(0)\) are considered fixed quantities, while \(W_i\) is a random variable.






Tip日本語訳





潜在結果枠組みには単位、処置、潜在結果の3つの主要要素がある。アングリスト（1990）が取り扱った問題を簡略化して考えてみよう。軍務が収入に及ぼす影響とは何か。この場合、単位は1970年の徴兵に適格だった米国人と定義でき、これらの人々を(i = 1, , N)でインデックス化できる。処置は「軍務に就く」または「軍務に就かない」であり、前者を処置条件、後者を対照条件と呼ぶ。処置条件の場合は(W_i = 1)、対照条件の場合は(W_i = 0)とする。最後に、潜在結果は「潜在」結果を含むため概念的に難しく、各1970年徴兵適格者は軍務に就いた場合と就かなかった場合の1978年の収入額をそれぞれ(Y_i(1))と(Y_i(0))と定義できる。潜在結果枠組みでは、(Y_i(1))と(Y_i(0))は固定量と見なし、(W_i)はランダム変数である。









Note理解のポイント





要点:潜在結果枠組みは単位、処置、潜在結果から構成され、1970年徴兵適格者の1978年の収入額を軍務に就いた場合と就かなかった場合の2つの潜在結果として定義する。





5The choice of units, treatments, and outcomes is critical because it defines what can—and cannot—be learned from the study. The choice of units—people eligible for the 1970 draft—does not include women, and so without additional assumptions, this study will not tell us anything about the effect of military service on women. Decisions about how to define treatments and outcomes are important as well. For example, should the treatment of interest be focused on serving in the military or experiencing combat? Should the outcome of interest be earnings or job satisfaction? Ultimately, the choice of units, treatments, and outcomes should be driven by the scientific and policy goals of the study.






Tip日本語訳





単位、処置、結果の選択は重要である理由は、それが研究から何が学べるか、また学べないかを定義するからである。単位の選択—1970年の徴兵に適格だった人々—には女性は含まれていないため、追加の仮定がない限り、この研究は軍務が女性に及ぼす影響について何も教えてくれないであろう。処置と結果をどのように定義するかについての決定も重要である。例えば、関心のある処置は軍務に従事することなのか、または戦闘を経験することなのか、関心のある結果は収入なのか、または仕事の満足度なのか、といった問いがある。最終的には、単位、処置、結果の選択は、研究の科学的および政策的目的によって駆動されるべきである。









Note理解のポイント





要点:単位、処置、結果の選択は研究の目的を定義し、その選択は科学的および政策的目的によって駆動されるべきである。





6Given the choices of units, treatments, and potential outcomes, the causal effect of the treatment on person \(i\), \(\tau_i\), is






Tip日本語訳





与えられた単位、処置、および潜在的な結果の選択肢を考えると、処置による個人(i)への因果効果(_i)は









Note理解のポイント





要点:因果効果(_i)は与えられた条件下での処置による個人への影響である





7\[ \tau_i = Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) \qquad(2.1)\]






Tip日本語訳





[ _i = Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) (2.1)]









Note理解のポイント





要点:処置効果(_i)は、個体(i)に対する処置の有無によって生じる差(Y_i(1) - Y_i(0))を表す。





8In other words, we compare how much person \(i\) would have earned after serving to how much person \(i\) would have earned without serving. To me, eq. 2.1 is the clearest way to define a causal effect, and although extremely simple, this framework turns out to generalizable in many important and interesting ways (Imbens and Rubin 2015).






Tip日本語訳





言い換えると、私たちは人物(i)が兵役に就いた場合と兵役に就かなかった場合の収入を比較します。私にとって、式2.1は因果効果を定義する最も明確な方法であり、非常にシンプルながらこのフレームワークは重要な多くの面で汎用性があることがわかりました（Imbens and Rubin 2015）。









Note理解のポイント





要点:式2.1は因果効果を定義する最も明確な方法であり、そのフレームワークは汎用性がある





9When using the potential outcomes framework, I often find it helpful to write out a table showing the potential outcomes and the treatment effects for all units (table 2.5). If you are not able to imagine a table like this for your study, then you might need to be more precise in your definitions of your units, treatments, and potential outcomes.






Tip日本語訳





潜在的結果フレームワークを使用する際には、研究の単位、処置、潜在的な結果を明確に定義するために、すべての単位に対する潜在的結果と処置効果を示した表（表2.5）を作成することが役立つことが多い。このような表を想像できない場合は、単位、処置、潜在的結果の定義をより明確にする必要があるかもしれない。









Note理解のポイント





要点:潜在的結果フレームワークを使用する際、単位、処置、潜在的結果の定義を明確にするための表の作成が役立つ。





10


Table 2.5: Table of Potential Outcomes

Earnings in treatment condition
Earnings in control condition
Treatment effect

\(Y_2(0)\)

\(\vdots\)
\(\vdots\)
\(\vdots\)

\(Y_N(0)\)
\(\tau_N\)

\(\bar{Y}(1)\)
\(\bar{Y}(0)\)

Tip日本語訳





表2.5: 予測結果の表 人物 処置条件での収入 対照条件での収入 処置効果 1 (Y_1(1)) (Y_1(0)) (_1) 2 (Y_2(1)) (Y_2(0)) (_2) () () () () N (Y_N(1)) (Y_N(0)) (_N) 平均 ({Y}(1)) ({Y}(0)) ({})









Note理解のポイント





要点:表は、各個人の処置条件と対照条件での収入、ならびにその処置効果を示している





11When defining the causal effect in this way, however, we run into a problem. In almost all cases, we don’t get to observe both potential outcomes. That is, a specific person either served or did not serve. Therefore, we observe one of the potential outcomes—\(Y_i(1)\) or \(Y_i(0)\)—but not both. The inability to observe both potential outcomes is such a major problem that Holland (1986) called it the Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference.






Tip日本語訳





このように因果効果を定義すると、両方の潜在的な結果を観察できないという重大な問題に直面します。つまり、特定の個人はサービスを受けたか受けなかったかのどちらかであり、その結果、(Y_i(1))または(Y_i(0))の一方のみを観察できますが、両方ではありません。この両方の潜在的な結果を観察できないことは、因果推論における基本的な問題と呼ばれています（Holland, 1986）。









Note理解のポイント





要点:両方の潜在的な結果を観察できないことが因果推論における基本的な問題である





12Fortunately, when we are doing research, we don’t just have one person; rather, we have many people, and this offers a way around the Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference. Instead of attempting to estimate the individual-level treatment effect, we can estimate the average treatment effect for all units:






Tip日本語訳





幸いなことに、研究を行う際には一人の人間ではなく、多くの人々が存在し、これは因果推論の基本問題に対する解決策を提供します。個々のレベルでの処置効果を推定しようとするのではなく、すべての単位に対する平均処置効果を推定することができます：









Note理解のポイント





要点:多くの人々を利用することで、個々のレベルでの処置効果ではなく、全体の平均処置効果を推定することが可能になる





13\[ \text{ATE} = \bar{\tau} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \tau_i \qquad(2.2)\]






Tip日本語訳





ATE = ({} = _{i=1}^N _i) (2.2)









Note理解のポイント





要点:平均処理効果(ATE)は、({} = _{i=1}^N _i)で定義される





14This equation is still expressed in terms of the \(\tau_i\), which are unobservable, but with some algebra (eq 2.8 of Gerber and Green (2012)), we get






Tip日本語訳





この方程式は依然として観測不能な(_i)を用いて表現されているが、いくつかの代数的変形（Gerber and Green (2012) の式 2.8）により、次のように得られる。









Note理解のポイント





要点:観測不能な(_i)を用いた方程式は代数的変形により別の形式を得られる





15\[ \text{ATE} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i(1) - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i(0) \qquad(2.3)\]






Tip日本語訳





平均処理効果（Average Treatment Effect: ATE）は、[ = {i=1}^N Y_i(1) - {i=1}^N Y_i(0) ]で与えられる。









Note理解のポイント





要点:平均処理効果（ATE）は、処理群と対照群の差の平均で定義される。





16This shows that if we can estimate the population average outcome under treatment (\(N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i(1)\)) and the population average outcome under control (\(N^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^N Y_i(1)\)), then we can estimate the average treatment effect, even without estimating the treatment effect for any particular person.






Tip日本語訳





これは、処置下の人口平均結果（(N^{-1} {i=1}^N Y_i(1))）と対照条件の人口平均結果（(N^{-1} {i=1}^N Y_i(0))）を推定できれば、個々の人の処置効果を推定せずに平均処置効果を推定できるということを示しています。









Note理解のポイント





要点:人口平均結果から平均処置効果を推定できる





17Now that I’ve defined our estimand—the thing we are trying to estimate—I’ll turn to how we can actually estimate it with data. And here we run directly into the problem that we only observe one of the potential outcomes for each person; we see either \(Y_i(0)\) or \(Y_i(1)\) (table 2.6). We could estimate the average treatment effect by comparing the earnings of people that served to the earnings of people that did not serve:






Tip日本語訳





私が定義した推定量、つまり我々が推定しようとしているものについて説明したので、次にデータを使ってそれを実際にどのように推定できるかについて述べる。ここで我々は直接問題に直面する、各個人について我々が観察できるのは潜在的な結果の一方のみであり、(Y_i(0))または(Y_i(1))のいずれかを見るだけである（表2.6を参照）。我々は、兵役に就いた人々の収入と兵役に就かなかった人々の収入を比較することで平均処置効果を推定できるだろう。









Note理解のポイント





要点:各個人の潜在的な結果の一方しか観察できないため、兵役に就いた人々と兵役に就かなかった人々の収入を比較して平均処置効果を推定する。





18\[ \widehat{\text{ATE}} = \underbrace{\frac{1}{N_t} \sum_{i:W_i=1} Y_i(1)}_{\text{average earnings, treatment}} - \underbrace{\frac{1}{N_c} \sum_{i:W_i=0} Y_i(0)}_{\text{average earnings, control}} \qquad(2.4)\]






Tip日本語訳





[ = {} - {} (2.4) ]









Note理解のポイント

23One approach to making causal estimates without running an experiment is to look for something happening in the world that has randomly assigned a treatment for you. This design is sometimes called an encouragement design. And the analysis method that I’ll describe to handle this situation is sometimes called instrumental variables. 45It turns out—somewhat surprisingly—that if there are any compliers, then provided one makes three additional assumptions, it is possible to estimate CACE from observed data. First, one has to assume that the assignment to treatment is random. In the case of the draft lottery this is reasonable. However, in some settings where natural experiments do not rely on physical randomization, this assumption may be more problematic. Second, one has to assume that their are no defiers (this assumption is also sometimes called the monotonicity assumption). In the context of the draft it seems reasonable to assume that there are very few people who will not serve if drafted and will serve if not drafted. Third, and finally, comes the most important assumption which is called the exclusion restriction. Under the exclusion restriction, one has to assume that all of the effect of the treatment assignment is passed through the treatment itself. In other words, one has to assume that there is no direct effect of encouragement on outcomes. In the case of the draft lottery, for example, one needs to assume that draft status has no effect on earnings other than through military service (figure 2.11). The exclusion restriction could be violated if, for example, people who were drafted spent more time in school in order to avoid service or if employers were less likely to hire people who were drafted.

CACEは、奨励された人々と奨励されなかった人々の結果の差を、処置受領率で拡大したものを指すと考えることができます。









Note理解のポイント





要点:CACEは、奨励された人々と奨励されなかった人々の結果の差を、処置受領率で拡大したものです。





52There are two important caveats to keep in mind. First, the exclusion restriction is a strong assumption, and it needs to be justified on a case-by-case basis, which frequently requires subject-area expertise. The exclusion restriction cannot be justified with randomization of the encouragement. Second, a common practical challenge with instrumental variable analysis comes when the encouragement has little effect on the uptake of treatment (when \(\text{ITT}_W\) is small). This is called a weak instrument, and it leads to a variety of problems (Imbens and Rosenbaum 2005; Murray 2006). One way to think about the problem with weak instruments is that \(\widehat{\text{CACE}}\) can be sensitive to small biases in \(\widehat{\text{ITT}_Y}\)—potentially due to violations of the exclusion restriction—because these biases get magnified by a small \(\widehat{\text{ITT}_W}\) (see eq. 2.13). Roughly, if the treatment that nature assigns doesn’t have a big impact on the treatment you care about, then you are going to have a hard time learning about the treatment you care about.






Tip日本語訳





二つの重要な注意点があります。第一に、除外制限は強い仮定であり、個々のケースごとに正当化する必要があります。これはしばしば専門分野の知識を必要とします。また、除外制限は奨励のランダム化によって正当化することはできません。第二に、操作変数分析における一般的な実務上の課題の一つは、奨励が処置の採用にほとんど影響を与えない場合（(_W)が小さい場合）です。これを弱い道具と呼び、これが様々な問題を引き起こします（Imbens and Rosenbaum 2005; Murray 2006）。弱い道具の問題を理解する一つの方法は、()の小さなバイアスが()が小さいために拡大され、結果として()が敏感になることです。つまり、自然が割り当てる処置が気にしている処置に大きな影響を与えない場合、気にしている処置について学ぶのは難しいということです。









Note理解のポイント





要点:除外制限の正当化と弱い道具による問題が指摘されている。





53See chapter 23 and 24 of Imbens and Rubin (2015) for a more formal version of this discussion. The traditional econometric approach to instrumental variables is typically expressed in terms of estimating equations, not potential outcomes. For an introduction from this other perspective, see Angrist and Pischke (2009), and for a comparison between the two approaches, see section 24.6 of Imbens and Rubin (2015). An alternative, slightly less formal presentation of the instrumental variables approach is provided in chapter 6 of Gerber and Green (2012). For more on the exclusion restriction, see D. Jones (2015). Aronow and Carnegie (2013) describe an additional set of assumptions that can be used to estimate ATE rather than CACE. For more on how natural experiments can be very tricky to interpret, see Sekhon and Titiunik (2012). For a more general introduction to natural experiments—one that goes beyond just the instrumental variables approach to also include designs such as regression discontinuity—see Dunning (2012).






Tip日本語訳





第23章と24章を参照してください（Imbens and Rubin, 2015）。伝統的な計量経済学における道具変数法は、潜在的結果ではなく推定方程式の観点から表現されることが一般的です。異なる視点からの導入については、Angrist and Pischke (2009)を参照してください。両者の方法を比較するには、Imbens and Rubin (2015)の第24.6節を参照してください。Gerber and Green (2012)の第6章では、やや形式性が低い道具変数法の説明が提供されています。除外制約についてさらに詳しく知りたい場合は、D. Jones (2015)を参照してください。Aronow and Carnegie (2013)は、ATEを推定するために使用できる追加の仮定セットを説明しています。自然実験が解釈するのが非常に難しい場合があることは、Sekhon and Titiunik (2012)で詳しく説明されています。より一般的な自然実験の導入については、回帰不連続デザインなど、単なる道具変数法を超えたアプローチも含むDunning (2012)を参照してください。









Note理解のポイント





要点:伝統的な計量経済学における道具変数法の解説と比較、自然実験の解釈の難しさ、さらには広範な自然実験のアプローチについての文献が紹介されている。







 Back to top

title: 2.4.3 Approximating experiments
text:
原文を開く ↗ · 日本語訳 29/29 段落 · 審校済み 0



2.4.3 Approximating experiments

1
We can approximate experiments that we haven’t or can’t do. Two approaches that especially benefit from big data sources are natural experiments and matching.







Tip日本語訳





私たちは実施できなかった実験を大規模データソースから特に恩恵を受けている自然実験やマッチングを利用して近似することができます。









Note理解のポイント





要点:大規模データソースを利用して自然実験やマッチングを行うことで、実施できない実験を近似できる。





2Some important scientific and policy questions are causal. For example, what is the effect of a job training program on wages? A researcher attempting to answer this question might compare the earnings of people who signed up for training to those that didn’t. But how much of any difference in wages between these groups is because of the training and how much is because of preexisting differences between the people that sign up and those that don’t? This is a difficult question, and it is one that doesn’t automatically go away with more data. In other words, the concern about possible preexisting differences arises no matter how many workers are in your data.






Tip日本語訳





重要な科学的および政策的な質問のいくつかは因果関係に関するものであり、例えば、職業訓練プログラムが賃金にどのような影響を与えるかという問いがある。研究者はこの問いに答えるために、訓練を受けた人々の収入と受けなかった人々の収入を比較するかもしれないが、これらのグループ間の賃金の差異のどれだけが訓練によるもので、どれだけが訓練を受けた人と受けなかった人との事前の違いによるものなのかは難しい問いであり、データの量が増えただけでは解決しない。つまり、事前の違いに関する懸念はデータに含まれる労働者の数に関わらず存在する。









Note理解のポイント





要点:訓練プログラムの効果を測定する際、事前の違いによる影響を排除することが難しい。





3In many situations, the strongest way to estimate the causal effect of some treatment, such as job training, is to run a randomized controlled experiment where a researcher randomly delivers the treatment to some people and not others. I’ll devote all of chapter 4 to experiments, so here I’m going to focus on two strategies that can be used with non-experimental data. The first strategy depends on looking for something happening in the world that randomly (or nearly randomly) assigns the treatment to some people and not others. The second strategy depends on statistically adjusting non-experimental data in an attempt to account for preexisting differences between those who did and did not receive the treatment.






Tip日本語訳





多くの状況では、ジョブトレーニングのような処置の因果効果を最も正確に推定する最善の方法は、研究者がランダムに一部の人々に処置を提供し、他の人々には提供しない無作為化比較試験を実施することである。第4章では実験に焦点を当てて説明するが、ここでは非実験データを使用する2つの戦略について述べる。第一の戦略は、世界で起こっている何かが処置を受ける人々と受けない人々をランダム（またはほぼランダム）に割り当てるような事象を見つけることに依存する。第二の戦略は、統計的に非実験データを調整し、処置を受けた人と受けなかった人との事前の違いを考慮に入れるよう試みることである。









Note理解のポイント





要点:非実験データを使用して因果効果を推定する2つの戦略について述べている。





4A skeptic might claim that both of these strategies should be avoided because they require strong assumptions, assumptions that are difficult to assess and that, in practice, are often violated. While I am sympathetic to this claim, I think it goes a bit too far. It is certainly true that it is difficult to reliably make causal estimates from non-experimental data, but I don’t think that means that we should never try. In particular, non-experimental approaches can be helpful if logistical constraint prevent you from conducting an experiment or if ethical constraints mean that you do not want to run an experiment. Further, non-experimental approaches can be helpful if you want to take advantage of data that already exist in order to design a randomized controlled experiment.






Tip日本語訳





懐疑的な人は、これらの両方の戦術が強い仮定を必要とするため、そのような仮定は評価が難しく、実際にはしばしば破られるため、両方の戦術を避けるべきだと主張するかもしれません。私はこの主張に同情的ですが、それは少し行き過ぎていると思います。非実験的データから因果関係を確実に推定することは確かに難しいですが、それが我々が決して試みるべきではないという意味ではありません。特に、実務上の制約により実験を行うことができない場合や、倫理的な制約により実験を実施したくない場合、非実験的手法は役立つことがあります。さらに、既存のデータを利用して無作為化比較試験を設計したい場合にも、非実験的手法は役立つことがあります。









Note理解のポイント





要点:非実験的手法は、実施や倫理的な制約がある場合や、既存データを活用したい場合に役立つが、強い仮定が必要であり評価が難しい。





5Before proceeding, it is also worth noting that making causal estimates is one of the most complex topics in social research, and one that can lead to intense and emotional debate. In what follows, I will provide an optimistic description of each approach in order to build intuition about it, then I will describe some of the challenges that arise when using that approach. Further details about each approach are available in the materials at the end of this chapter. If you plan to use either of these approaches in your own research, I highly recommend reading one of the many excellent books on causal inference (Imbens and Rubin 2015; Pearl 2009; Morgan and Winship 2014).






Tip日本語訳





因果推定は社会研究において最も複雑なトピックの一つであり、それが引き起こす激しい感情的な議論もまた注目に値する。以下では各アプローチについて楽観的な説明を行い直感を養い、その後そのアプローチを使用する際に生じる課題について述べる。各アプローチに関する詳細はこの章の最後の資料を参照のこと。自身の研究でこれらのアプローチを使用する予定がある場合は因果推定に関する優れた本（Imbens and Rubin 2015；Pearl 2009；Morgan and Winship 2014）のいずれかを読むことを強く推奨する。









Note理解のポイント





要点:因果推定は社会研究で最も複雑で議論の多いトピックであり、その使用には課題がある。





6One approach to making causal estimates from non-experimental data is to look for an event that has randomly assigned a treatment to some people and not to others. These situations are called natural experiments. One of the clearest examples of a natural experiment comes from the research of Joshua Angrist (1990) measuring the effect of military services on earnings. During the war in Vietnam, the United States increased the size of its armed forces through a draft. In order to decide which citizens would be called into service, the US government held a lottery. Every birth date was written on a piece of paper, and, as shown in figure 2.7, these pieces of paper were selected one at a time in order to determine the order in which young men would be called to serve (young women were not subject to the draft). Based on the results, men born on September 14 were called first, men born on April 24 were called second, and so on. Ultimately, in this lottery, men born on 195 different days were drafted, while men born on 171 days were not.






Tip日本語訳





非実験データから因果推定を行う方法の一つとして、ある事象がランダムに一部の人々に処置を与え、他の人々には与えない場合がある。このような状況は自然実験と呼ばれる。ジョシュア・アングリスト（1990）の研究は、ベトナム戦争中のアメリカの徴兵制度を通じて、軍務が収入に及ぼす影響を測定する際の最も明確な自然実験の例を提供している。当時、アメリカ政府は、抽選によってどの市民が召集されるかを決定した。図2.7に示すように、各出生日が書かれた紙が順番に引き出され、若い男性の召集順序が決まった（若い女性は徴兵の対象ではなかった）。その結果、9月14日に生まれた男性が最初に召集され、4月24日に生まれた男性が次に召集され、最終的に195日生まれの男性が召集され、171日生まれの男性は召集されなかった。









Note理解のポイント





要点:ベトナム戦争時のアメリカの徴兵制度は、出生日による抽選によって収入への影響を測る自然実験となった。





7

Figure 2.7: Congressman Alexander Pirnie (R-NY) drawing the first capsule for the Selective Service draft on December 1, 1969. Joshua Angrist (1990) combined the draft lottery with earnings data from the Social Security Administration to estimate the effect of military service on earnings. This is an example of research using a natural experiment. Source: U.S. Selective Service System (1969)/Wikimedia Commons.







Tip日本語訳





図2.7：1969年12月1日、ニューヨーク州選出の議員アレクサンダー・ピルニー（共和党）が当時の徴兵抽選で最初のカプセルを引く様子。Joshua Angrist（1990）は、社会保障庁の収入データと徴兵抽選を組み合わせて軍務が収入に及ぼす影響を推定した。これは自然実験を利用した研究の例である。出典：U.S. Selective Service System（1969）/Wikimedia Commons。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Angristは徴兵抽選と収入データを組み合わせて軍務の収入への影響を推定した。





8Although it might not be immediately apparent, a draft lottery has a critical similarity to a randomized controlled experiment: in both situations, participants are randomly assigned to receive a treatment. In order to study the effect of this randomized treatment, Angrist took advantage of an always-on big data system: the US Social Security Administration, which collects information on virtually every American’s earnings from employment. By combining the information about who was randomly selected in the draft lottery with the earnings data that was collected in governmental administrative records, Angrist concluded that the earnings of veterans were about 15% less than the earnings of comparable non-veterans.






Tip日本語訳





確かに直ちには明らかではないが、ドラフト抽選は無作為化比較試験と重要な類似点がある：両方の状況で参加者はランダムに処置を受けるグループに割り当てられる。このランダム化された処置の効果を研究するために、Angristは常に稼働している大規模データシステムである米国社会安全保障庁を活用した：これは実質的にすべてのアメリカ人の収入情報を収集している。ドラフト抽選でランダムに選ばれた人々の情報と政府の行政記録で収集された収入データを組み合わせることで、Angristは退役軍人の収入が類似の非退役軍人よりも約15%少ないことを結論付けた。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Angristは、米国社会安全保障庁のデータを使用して、退役軍人の収入が類似の非退役軍人よりも約15%少ないことを結論付けた。





9As this example illustrates, sometimes social, political, or natural forces assign treatments in a way that can be leveraged by researchers, and sometimes the effects of these treatments are captured in always-on big data sources. This research strategy can be summarized as follows: \[\text{random (or as if random) variation} + \text{always-on data} = \text{natural experiment}\]






Tip日本語訳





この例が示すように、社会的、政治的、または自然の力によって処置が割り当てられ、研究者がそれを利用できる場合があり、またその処置の効果が常にオンの大きなデータソースにキャプチャされることがあります。この研究戦略は以下のようになります：[ランダム（またはランダムに近い）変動 + 常にオンのデータ = 自然実験]









Note理解のポイント





要点:社会的、政治的、自然の力による処置の割り当てと常にオンの大きなデータソースの組み合わせが自然実験を形成する





10To illustrate this strategy in the digital age, let’s consider a study by Alexandre Mas and Enrico Moretti (2009) that tried to estimate the effect of working with productive colleagues on a worker’s productivity. Before seeing the results, it is worth pointing out that there are conflicting expectations that you might have. On the one hand, you might expect that working with productive colleagues would lead a worker to increase her productivity because of peer pressure. Or, on the other hand, you might expect that having hard-working peers might lead a worker to slack off because the work will be done by her peers anyway. The clearest way to study peer effects on productivity would be a randomized controlled experiment where workers are randomly assigned to shifts with workers of different productivity levels and then the resulting productivity is measured for everyone. Researchers, however, do not control the schedule of workers in any real business, and so Mas and Moretti had to rely on a natural experiment involving cashiers at a supermarket.






Tip日本語訳





デジタル時代におけるこの戦略を説明するために、Alexandre MasとEnrico Moretti（2009）の研究を考えてみよう。彼らは生産的な同僚と働くことによる労働者の生産性への影響を推定しようと試みた。結果を見る前に、予想が分かれる点があることに注意が必要だ。一方では、同僚からのプレッシャーにより労働者の生産性が向上すると予想されるかもしれないし、他方では同僚が頑張れば自分は楽をできると考えて生産性が低下するかもしれない。最も明確な方法は、労働者を異なる生産性レベルの同僚とランダムに割り当て、その結果としての生産性を測定する無作為化比較試験だが、研究者は実際のビジネスで労働者のスケジュールをコントロールできないため、MasとMorettiはスーパーマーケットのレジ係を対象とした自然実験に依頼した。









Note理解のポイント





要点:Alexandre MasとEnrico Morettiの研究は、生産的な同僚と働くことで労働者の生産性がどう変わるかを自然実験で探った。





11In this particular supermarket, because of the way that scheduling was done and the way that shifts overlapped, each cashier had different co-workers at different times of day. Further, in this particular supermarket, the assignment of cashiers was unrelated to the productivity of their peers or how busy the store was. In other words, even though the scheduling of cashiers was not determined by a lottery, it was as if workers were sometimes randomly assigned to work with high (or low) productivity peers. Fortunately, this supermarket also had a digital-age checkout system that tracked the items that each cashier was scanning at all times. From this checkout log data, Mas and Moretti were able to create a precise, individual, and always-on measure of productivity: the number of items scanned per second. Combining these two things—the naturally occurring variation in peer productivity and the always-on measure of productivity—Mas and Moretti estimated that if a cashier was assigned co-workers who were 10% more productive than average, her productivity would increase by 1.5%. Further, they used the size and richness of their data to explore two important issues: the heterogeneity of this effect (For which kinds of workers is the effect larger?) and the mechanisms behind the effect (Why does having high-productivity peers lead to higher productivity?). We will return to these two important issues—heterogeneity of treatment effects and mechanisms—in chapter 4 when we discuss experiments in more detail.






Tip日本語訳





この特定のスーパーマーケットでは、スケジューリングの方法とシフトの重複の仕方により、各レジ係員は一日の異なる時間帯で異なる同僚を持つことになった。さらに、この特定のスーパーマーケットでは、レジ係員の配置は同僚の生産性や店の混雑度とは無関係だった。言い換えれば、レジ係員のスケジューリングがくじ引きによって決定されたわけではなく、労働者は時として高（または低）生産性の同僚とランダムに一緒に働くことになったのである。幸いにも、このスーパーマーケットにはレジ係員がいつでもスキャンしている商品を追跡するデジタル時代のレジシステムがあった。このレジログデータから、マスとモレッティは、レジ係員がスキャンするアイテム数を秒単位で測定する正確で個人別の常にオンの生産性指標を作成した。これらの2つの要素—自然に発生する同僚の生産性の変動と常にオンの生産性の測定—を組み合わせて、もしレジ係員が平均より10%高い生産性を持つ同僚と配属された場合、彼女の生産性は1.5%向上するとマスとモレッティは推定した。さらに、彼らはデータの大きさと豊かさを利用して、この効果の異質性（どの種類の労働者に対して効果が大きいのか？）と効果のメカニズム（なぜ高生産性の同僚を持つと生産性が上がるのか？）という2つの重要な問題を探った。我々は、処置効果の異質性とメカニズムという2つの重要な問題について、詳細な実験の議論をする第4章で再び戻る。









Note理解のポイント





要点:マスとモレッティは、レジ係員の生産性が同僚の生産性に影響を受け、10%高い生産性を持つ同僚と配属されると1.5%向上すると推定した。





12Generalizing from these two studies, table 2.3 summarizes other studies that have this same structure: using an always-on data source to measure the effect of some random variation. In practice, researchers use two different strategies for finding natural experiments, both of which can be fruitful. Some researchers start with an always-on data source and look for random events in the world; others start a random event in the world and look for data sources that capture its impact.






Tip日本語訳





これらの2つの研究から一般化し、表2.3は同じ構造を持つ他の研究をまとめている。実際には、研究者は自然実験を見つけるために2つの異なる戦略を使い、どちらも有益である。一部の研究者は常にデータ源を使用して世界のランダムなイベントを探す一方、他の研究者は世界のランダムなイベントから始めてその影響をキャプチャするデータ源を探す。









Note理解のポイント





要点:研究者は自然実験を見つけるために、常にデータ源を使用して世界のランダムなイベントを探すか、または世界のランダムなイベントから始めてその影響をキャプチャするデータ源を探す。





13

14In the discussion so far about natural experiments, I’ve left out an important point: going from what nature has provided to what you want can sometimes be quite tricky. Let’s return to the Vietnam draft example. In this case, Angrist was interested in estimating the effect of military service on earnings. Unfortunately, military service was not randomly assigned; rather it was being drafted that was randomly assigned. However, not everyone who was drafted served (there were a variety of exemptions), and not everyone who served was drafted (people could volunteer to serve). Because being drafted was randomly assigned, a researcher can estimate the effect of being drafted for all men in the draft. But Angrist didn’t want to know the effect of being drafted; he wanted to know the effect of serving in the military. To make this estimate, however, additional assumptions and complications are required. First, researchers need to assume that the only way that being drafted impacted earnings is through military service, an assumption called the exclusion restriction. This assumption could be wrong if, for example, men who were drafted stayed in school longer in order to avoid serving or if employers were less likely to hire men who were drafted. In general, the exclusion restriction is a critical assumption, and it is usually hard to verify. Even if the exclusion restriction is correct, it is still impossible to estimate the effect of service on all men. Instead, it turns out that researchers can only estimate the effect on a specific subset of men called compliers (men who would serve when drafted, but would not serve when not drafted) (Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin 1996). Compliers, however, were not the original population of interest. Notice that these problems arise even in the relatively clean case of the draft lottery. A further set of complications arise when the treatment is not assigned by a physical lottery. For example, in Mas and Moretti’s study of cashiers, additional questions arise about the assumption that the assignment of peers is essentially random. If this assumption were strongly violated, it could bias their estimates. To conclude, natural experiments can be a powerful strategy for making causal estimates from non-experimental data, and big data sources increase our ability to capitalize on natural experiments when they occur. However, it will probably require great care—and sometimes strong assumptions—to go from what nature has provided to the estimate that you want.

15The second strategy I’d like to tell you about for making causal estimates from non-experimental data depends on statistically adjusting non-experimental data in an attempt to account for preexisting differences between those who did and did not receive the treatment. There are many such adjustment approaches, but I’ll focus on one called matching. In matching, the researcher looks through non-experimental data to create pairs of people who are similar except that one has received the treatment and one has not. In the process of matching, researchers are actually also pruning; that is, discarding cases where there are no obvious match. Thus, this method would be more accurately called matching-and-pruning, but I’ll stick with the traditional term: matching.

18If you are already aware of the problems that can arise when making causal estimates from non-experimental data, you might skip the naive approach and consider running a field experiment where you would sell a specific item—say, a golf club—with a fixed set of auction parameters—say, free shipping and auction open for two weeks—but with randomly assigned starting prices. By comparing the resulting market outcomes, this field experiment would offer a very clear measurement of the effect of starting price on sale price. But this measurement would only apply to one particular product and set of auction parameters. The results might be different, for example, for different types of products. Without a strong theory, it is difficult to extrapolate from this single experiment to the full range of possible experiments that could have been run. Further, field experiments are sufficiently expensive that it would be infeasible to run every variation that you might want to try.

22Recall that Einav and colleagues were interested in the effect of start price on auction outcomes. First, they used linear regression to estimate that higher starting prices decrease the probability of a sale, and that higher starting prices increase the final sale price (conditional on a sale occurring). By themselves, these estimates—which describe a linear relationship and are averaged over all products—are not all that interesting. Then, Einav and colleagues used the massive size of their data to create a variety of more subtle estimates. For example, by estimating the effect separately for a variety of different starting prices, they found that the relationship between starting price and sale price is nonlinear (figure 2.9). In particular, for starting prices between 0.05 and 0.85, the starting price has very little impact on sale price, a finding that was completely missed by their first analysis. Further, rather than averaging over all items, Einav and colleagues estimated the impact of starting price for 23 different categories of items (e.g., pet supplies, electronics, and sports memorabilia) (figure 2.10). These estimates show that for more distinctive items—such as memorabilia—starting price has a smaller effect on the probability of a sale and a larger effect on the final sale price. Further, for more commodified items—such as DVDs—the starting price has almost no impact on the final price. In other words, an average that combines results from 23 different categories of items hides important differences between these items.
